newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo Jan-July iron output nine-fold up.
newsitem.headline: Yugo Jan-July iron output nine-fold up.

text.p: Yugoslavia's iron production leapt nine-fold and steel output climbed three and a half times in the first seven months this year, the Association of Yugoslav Steelers said on Tuesday.
"The iron and steel producers are almost meeting set outputs," association official Savo Markovic told Reuters.
He said iron production climbed to 227,886 tonnes in January to July this year, up from 22,593 over the same period in 1995.
Steel production in the first seven months reached 293,511 tonnes, more than triple the previous year's output of 81,069 tonnes.

Yugoslavia's largest steel works, Sartid of Smederevo was responsible for much of the increase, lifting production to 222,676 tonnes of steel in the January-July period from 25,138 tonnes against the same period last year. Markovic described the increase as significant.
In the same period, another steel plant in Niksic produced 70,835 tonnes of steel, up from 55,931 tonnes.

In total, the Smederevo and Niksic plants and eight other steel processors also tripled their production of finished goods in the first seven months of the year, turning out 334,128 tonnes over 114,166 tonnes for the same period in 1995. -- Gordana Kukic, Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
